paper.title: Are sample means in multi-armed bandits positively or negatively biased?

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic MAB framework with adaptive sampling, stopping and choosing (bias of the sample mean)
unmapped: Guarantee is on the sign of the bias of the sample mean of an adaptively chosen arm at an adaptive stopping time, not on regret
Arm distributions are arbitrary with finite means
Experiment is agnostic to its aim (regret minimisation, BAI, etc.)
settings.definition_quote: Let $P_1, \dots, P_K$ be $K$ distributions of interest (also called arms) with finite means $\mu_k = \E_{Y\sim P_k}[Y]$. ... The phrase ``fully adaptive setting'' refers to the scenario of running an adaptive sampling algorithm until an adaptive stopping time $\Tau$, and asking about the sample mean of an adaptively chosen arm $\kappa$.

algorithms.name: Any monotonically decreasing data collecting strategy (e.g. optimistic sampling with nonadaptive stopping and choosing)
Any monotonically increasing data collecting strategy (e.g. optimistic stopping or optimistic choosing)

conditions: for all k with P(kappa=k)>0: E[N_k(T)] < infinity and N_k(T) >= 1 (E[N_k] finiteness can be dropped for bounded arms)
data collecting strategy is monotonically decreasing

source.label: thm::bias_sign
source.quote: If the data collecting strategy is monotonically decreasing, for example under optimistic sampling with nonadaptive stopping and choosing, then we have \E\left[ \hat{\mu}_\kappa (\Tau)\mid \kappa = k \right] \leq \mu_k ... which also implies that \E\left[ \hat{\mu}_\kappa(\Tau) - \mu_\kappa \right] \leq 0.

results.notes: Bound is on the bias of the sample mean (quantity 'other'), not regret. Also holds conditionally on kappa=k for each k.

conditions: for all k with P(kappa=k)>0: E[N_k(T)] < infinity and N_k(T) >= 1 (E[N_k] finiteness can be dropped for bounded arms)
data collecting strategy is monotonically increasing

source.label: thm::bias_sign
source.quote: Similarly if the data collecting strategy is monotonically increasing, for example under optimistic stopping with nonadaptive sampling and choosing, or under optimistic choosing with nonadaptive sampling and stopping, then we have \E\left[ \hat{\mu}_\kappa(\Tau)\mid \kappa = k \right] \geq \mu_k ... \E\left[ \hat{\mu}_\kappa(\Tau) - \mu_\kappa \right] \geq 0.

results.notes: Lower bound on the bias (positive bias) for a class of strategies, not a minimax lower bound.

conditions: algorithm is lil'UCB (sampling, stopping and choosing rules of Jamieson et al. 2014)
conditions of Theorem 7 (finite means, E[N_k(T)] < infinity, N_k(T) >= 1)

source.label: cor::lil'UCB
source.quote: The lil'UCB algorithm is a monotonically increasing strategy, and thus the sample mean of the reported arm when lil'UCB stops is always positively biased.

results.notes: Sign-of-bias statement for lil'UCB; not a regret or sample complexity bound.
